questions.question: Which design direction do you want for the site?

options.label: Refined dark minimal (Recommended)
options.description: Keep a dark, developer-flavored identity but strip the cyberpunk gimmicks: no glitch/scan-lines/orbs, one accent color, strong typography, readable article pages. Content becomes the hero.
options.preview:
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Xiaofeng Xie          Blog Books Tools│
│                                      │
│  Hi, I'm Xiaofeng.                   │
│  Software engineer writing about     │
│  frontend architecture & tooling.    │
│                                      │
│  Recent writing                      │
│  ────────────────                    │
│  Thoughts on Module Federation 2.0   │
│  Jun 2024 · architecture             │
│                                      │
│  Solving multi-app integration…      │
│  Mar 2024 · module-federation        │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
Dark background, one cyan accent used
sparingly, clean Inter type, generous
whitespace. Quiet, professional.

options.label: Polish the cyberpunk theme
options.description: Keep the neon/terminal aesthetic as the identity, but fix contrast, remove fake stats, reduce effect overload, and improve article readability within the theme.

content.text:
The redesign is done and verified. I rebuilt the site's design around the "refined dark minimal" direction you picked — every page now puts content first, and I confirmed it all renders correctly in the browser with no console errors.

**What changed:**

- **Design system** (`src/tailwind.css`) — went from ~900 lines to ~150. New palette: near-black background, a single cyan accent (`#22d3ee`), and a muted text color that actually passes contrast (`#9aa3b2` vs. the old `#5a5a7a`). Removed all 20 cyberpunk animations (glitch, scan lines, shimmer, particles, CRT, holographic…), keeping just a subtle fade-in, a shared `.card` style, and visible focus outlines for keyboard users.
- **Home page** — replaced the "READ THINK CODE" hero, fake terminal, fake stats ("500+ COMMITS", lat/lon coordinates), and mousemove-driven parallax with a plain intro, your three most recent posts (loaded from real blog data), and two cards linking to the reading list and tools. This also removed the per-pixel re-render performance problem.
- **Blog list & article pages** — the list is now a clean date + title + excerpt layout; articles get a narrower 3xl reading column with proper typography, styled inline code and blockquotes, and none of the "END_OF_TRANSMISSION" chrome. The 404 page is similarly simplified (I verified it renders by hitting a bad slug).
- **Header/footer** — slim sticky header with your name, three nav links with active-state highlighting, and the ⌘K search trigger; footer is one line plus social icons. Dropped the "ONLINE" status badge and the contradictory version numbers.
- **Command palette** — kept all the search/AI functionality, just restyled the shell (rounded card, calm labels instead of "SYSTEM // COMMAND_AGENT v2.0").
- **Dead code removed** — `components/effects/` (FloatingOrbs, GlitchText, TiltCard, MatrixRain), `components/Card/` (BlogCard/ToolCard were unused by any route), and `components/ui/Button.tsx`, plus the ToolCard test that only covered the dead component.
- Small bonuses: the tools page now actually groups by category (the old code computed categories but rendered a flat list), and reading-list/tools pages got proper `<title>`/meta tags.

**Validation:** `vp check` passes (format, lint, typecheck), all 13 remaining tests pass, and I screenshotted every page plus the ⌘K palette on a live dev server — all render correctly with zero console errors.

The changes are uncommitted on `main`. If you'd like, I can commit them on a branch, or make adjustments first — for example, the accent color is one variable in `tailwind.css` if cyan isn't your taste.
